definition: Forward displacement is the tendency to remember the last seen position of a moving object as slightly farther along its path than it actually was. In this context, it reflects an anticipatory perception of the object’s near-future state.

reasons: The packet does not define “forward displacement” as a general “tendency to remember the last seen position” of a moving object; it discusses representational momentum (RM) as a forward displacement of a memory representation of a moving object’s final position in a specific taekwondo video task.

The definition’s phrasing “slightly farther along its path than it actually was” is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet only describes RM as a “forward displacement” of the memory representation without providing the “last seen” vs “actual” comparison in those terms.

While the packet says RM “implies that observers perceptually ‘see’ a near future forthcoming dynamic environmental state,” the definition adds additional framing (“In this context… anticipatory perception of the object’s near-future state”) that is partially supported by that implication, but other core claims about what is remembered and compared are not supported.
